title: Edge Surge Provisioning Workbench — Private VPC Capacity & BOM (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This workbook collects the heuristics, quick formulas and reference BOM lines we use to size small regional (edge) GPU pools that act as 'surge shelters' for Private/VPC deployments. Goal is to give SEs and customers a fast estimate they can iterate on during onboarding and procurement conversations.

Audience / context:
- For solutions engineering and capacity planning for Private deployments where a full regional fleet is excessive but burst isolation and low-latency regional routing are required.
- Meant to be a living draft: conservative defaults, with knobs for model perf, prompt length, prewarm strategy, and safety margins.

High-level approach (one-line):
Calculate baseline steady-state GPU count from expected concurrent request load, add burst headroom for X-minute surges, add redundancy + spare units for preemption/maintenance, then translate into rack/host/SKU BOM and networking/power margins.

Inputs (editable):
- peak_rps: peak requests per second (regional) — default 150
- avg_tokens_per_request: 120 tokens
- model_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu: 300 tokens/sec (depends on model/quantization/HW)
- avg_concurrency_per_request: 1.0 (assume single-stream)
- desired_tail_latency_slo_ms: 250ms (target for 95th)
- surge_window_minutes: 5 (time window we want to absorb without scaling)
- surge_multiplier: 2.5 (how much above peak to plan for)
- spare_fraction: 0.12 (12% spares for maintenance/failures/preempt)
- prewarm_instances: 1 per 8 GPUs (hosts with warmed CUDA context)

Key formulas (text):
- tokens_per_second_demand = peak_rps * avg_tokens_per_request
- baseline_gpus = ceil(tokens_per_second_demand / model_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu)
- surge_gpus = ceil(baseline_gpus * (surge_multiplier - 1))
- raw_required_gpus = baseline_gpus + surge_gpus
- required_gpus_with_spares = ceil(raw_required_gpus * (1 + spare_fraction))
- hosts_needed = ceil(required_gpus_with_spares / gpus_per_host)
- prewarm_hosts = ceil(hosts_needed / 8) * prewarm_instances_per_8 (configurable)

Default example (walkthrough):
- Inputs: peak_rps=150, avg_tokens_per_request=120, model_tps_per_gpu=300
- tokens_per_second_demand = 150 * 120 = 18,000 tps
- baseline_gpus = ceil(18,000 / 300) = 60 GPUs
- surge_multiplier = 2.5 => surge_gpus = ceil(60 * 1.5) = 90 GPUs
- raw_required_gpus = 60 + 90 = 150 GPUs
- spare_fraction 12% => required_gpus_with_spares = ceil(150 * 1.12) = 168 GPUs
- If we pick 8x A100-style hosts (8 GPUs/host), hosts_needed = ceil(168 / 8) = 21 hosts
- prewarm_hosts (1 per 8 GPUs) = ceil(21 / 8) = 3 prewarm hosts (adjustable)

Scenario buckets (quick presets):
- Conservative (S1): surge_multiplier=1.25, spare_fraction=0.08 -> smaller BOM, lower capex; for low-SLA internal workloads.
- Baseline (S2): surge_multiplier=1.75, spare_fraction=0.12 -> recommended default for customer pilots.
- Aggressive/Resilient (S3): surge_multiplier=2.5, spare_fraction=0.2 -> enterprise-grade with large safety buffers.

SKU and BOM reference (example lines) — local procurement names replaced with vendor-agnostic descriptors:
- GPU host (8xA100-40GB equivalent) — per-host list price: $120k (rack-ready blade, includes chassis). Rack density: 8 GPUs/host.
- GPU host (4xH100 80GB equiv) — per-host list price: $95k (higher perf/less density).
- NVMe local storage 4TB per host — $2k
- 100Gbps NIC + SmartNIC offload — $3.5k per host
- Top-of-Rack 100Gbps switch port — $900 per 100G port (estimate share)
- Rack PDU & power cabling (per rack) — $6k
- Networking spine charges / cross-AZ link sticker — estimated $8k monthly per region (highly variable)
- KMS/HSM hardware or SLA uplift (for private keys/attestation) — consult security pricing

Sample cost calc (derived from defaults above):
- Using 21 hosts (8x GPU): hardware capex = 21 * $120k = $2.52M
- NVMe/storage = 21 * $2k = $42k
- NICs = 21 * $3.5k = $73.5k
- Rack PDUs & misc (assume 1 rack can hold up to 10 hosts) -> 3 racks -> 3 * $6k = $18k
- Switch ports/spine etc -> placeholder $60k provisioning (one-time infra)
- One-year ops estimate (power/cooling/colocation) -> annualized $350k (depends on region)
- Notes: discounts and OEM pricing reduce CAPEX by 15-35% typically; we should provide range rather than single number during customer proposals.

Placement and topology notes (edge/surge shelter specifics):
- Keep shelters small and geographically distributed: prefer many 10–30 host pools instead of single larger region when low-latency regional routing is primary requirement.
- Use prewarm lanes: keep 1–3 hosts per pool in warm state (CUDA contexts loaded) to accept first-wave cold requests while autoscaling adds hosts.
- Cache KV/LLM prefix caches on hosts to reduce token cost during surge windows (prefix caching reduces tokens/second demand for repeated prompts).
- Multi-tier routing: regional shelter -> regional main pool -> central fallback. Configure SLO-based routing with soft-fallback so requests spill to central only after X% saturation or latency breach.

Operational considerations and failure modes:
- Preemption (cloud) or NV failure (on-prem) -> spare_fraction aims to cover single-host failures. For N+1 across racks, increase spare fraction.
- Network congestion: heavy bursty traffic requires NIC oversubscription planning; plan for at least 1.2x network headroom on ToR->spine links.
- Model version drift / quantization mismatch -> keep staging set of hosts for canary model testing.

Quick checklist for SE to run in customer call:
1) Confirm expected peak_rps and avg_tokens (ask product team for sample traffic).
2) Decide acceptable tail_latency and surge_window.
3) Pick a scenario preset (S1/S2/S3).
4) Compute GPUs/hosts and map to customer's preferred SKUs and rack constraints.
5) Draft BOM and a 3-year TCO with maintenance and expected cloud/network fees.
6) Flag security/compliance lines (KMS, on-site HSM, network isolation) to legal & security for pricing adjustments.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate default model_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu numbers vs our latest perf-bench (ask Applied ML for latest tps by model family).
- Add a host-level power/cooling model (W per GPU + overhead) to compute colocation power quotes more precisely.
- Add a preemption cost model for hybrid clouds (spot replacement latency and tail latency impacts).

References & notes:
- Shortcuts in this sheet are intended for quick feasibility conversations; final procurement requires full vendor quotes and on-site power/cooling validation.
- Related internal pages: Edge Surge Patterns (Confluence), Private VPC Ops runbook (link above).

Notes to self (drafty):
- Consider adding CSV export for quick import into the pricing workbook.
- Add a column for 'deploy friction' (customer readiness to accept on-prem racks) to help prioritize S2 vs S3.
- Run 3 customer pilots with the 'shelter' approach in EMEA to validate latency and fault domains before recommending broadly.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-03 created by Ava Chen (initial heuristics)
- 2025-12-12 updated: added SKU cost placeholders and scenario presets (Diego)
- 2026-02-12 updated: adjusted defaults (surge_multiplier -> 2.5 for S3), added prewarm note (Priya)
